subject: Starlite Health - PO field validation, invoice rail limits, and pre-bill exception request
messages:
From: John Keane <john.keane@starlitehealth.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@starlitehealth.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: PO fields + invoice cadence constraints for Redwood

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement reviewed the SOW and we have two blocking items before legal/finance can accept the vendor setup: a strict PO header layout and an invoice cadence restriction (we can only accept monthly invoices unless there's documented pre-bill approval).

Specifically, our AP system requires: PO_ID (alphanumeric max 20), LineItem_SKU, Contract Entity ID (our ERP entity), and Tax Jurisdiction code. If any of those are missing we route the invoice to manual queue and it delays payment by 30–45 days.

We attached our PO template and an example XML export that our ERP will generate. Two asks:
1) Can Redwood include PO_ID on the invoice PDF metadata AND in the line-level CSV we deliver?
2) We rarely allow weekly or ad-hoc invoices — can you confirm Redwood supports monthly consolidated billing? If not, we need to request a pre-bill exception through our vendor governance (takes ~2 weeks).

If the vendor can accept monthly invoices and the PO fields, procurement will expedite the registration and move to legal. Otherwise we need to escalate for an exception.

Thanks,
John Keane
Director, Strategic Procurement
Starlite Health

Attachments: Starlite_PO_Template_v3.pdf (pdf), Starlite_PO_Example_12345.xml (xml)
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: John Keane <john.keane@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO fields + invoice cadence constraints for Redwood

John —

Appreciate the clear list and the template. Short answers up front: yes to PO_ID on both invoice PDF metadata and line-level CSV, and yes we support consolidated monthly billing by default. We do also support weekly invoices for customers on high-frequency consumption plans but that is explicitly opt-in.

A couple of details and options for your team to consider:
- Invoice metadata: we can inject PO_ID into the PDF header and add a 'po_id' column in our line-item CSV export.
- Line-level SKUs: we map internal model SKUs to external SKUs; we can provide a mapping file as part of onboarding.
- Entity mapping: we need the exact ERP entity ID and GL mapping; if you provide a sample export we will mirror those fields exactly.
- Pre-bill exceptions: if Starlite needs invoices more frequently for cashflow, we can approve weekly billing but we would need a signed addendum that outlines the billing lane and a short-term credit holdback (standard risk protection).

I'll coordinate with Finance to document the default monthly cadence and the template we will use. Vanessa — can you confirm the impact to revenue recognition and whether any manual steps are needed from our end to include Tax Jurisdiction code? Vivek — could you weigh in on the addendum language for a temporary weekly pre-bill lane and the holdback percentage you typically require?

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement this week.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Diego / Vivek —

Quick finance note: including PO_ID in both the invoice PDF header and the CSV is fine — our billing pipeline supports a "po_id" metadata field and a mapped CSV column. Revenue recognition is unaffected if invoices are consolidated monthly.

If Starlite requests a weekly pre-bill lane we will request a 30-day holdback (percentage tiers depend on ARR commitment; for new enterprise customers we usually hold 10% until two consecutive months of on-time payment). This protects us from delayed clears in their ERP. We can also offer a 0.5% early-pay discount if they move from net45 to net30 on their master purchase order.

I will prepare a short addendum template that covers: billing cadence, holdback %, early-pay discount, and required PO fields. Diego — please confirm whether you want me to send the addendum now with "monthly default" language and a conditional weekly lane, or wait for procurement to formally request the exception.

-Vanessa
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO fields + invoice cadence constraints for Redwood

John / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick feedback. To keep momentum and avoid adding another governance cycle, here's a short mutual action plan from Redwood: 

1) We will deliver invoices with PO_ID in the PDF header and a line-level CSV that includes: po_id, lineitem_sku, contract_entity_id, tax_jurisdiction_code.
2) Default cadence will be monthly consolidated invoices (first invoice on the 1st of the month, payment due net45 unless you accept the early-pay discount).
3) If Starlite needs weekly pre-billing, Redwood can enable a weekly lane for the first 90 days under a temporary addendum: 10% holdback until 2 months of on-time payment, or a reduced holdback of 5% if Starlite signs up for a 12-month committed spend band.
4) Finance will include a 0.5% early-pay discount if Starlite revises the PO payment term to net30.

Next steps: John — if that sounds acceptable please reply with your ERP entity IDs and confirm whether you want to pursue weekly pre-billing or stay on monthly by default. Vanessa will attach the short addendum and Vivek will draft the simple billing mapping file we need for onboarding. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to finalize.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to getting this closed.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments sent: Starlite_PO_Template_v3.pdf (kept for reference)
